correctness.rationale: An explicit Johnson association-scheme diagonalization yields the degree-one and degree-two distance eigenvalues; the distance matrix is an exact affine combination of I, J, A1 and A2. For \(0<p\le1\), three positive factored differences prove E3 is strictly maximal; its derivative is strictly positive and endpoint values have opposite signs. Negative-type exponents form an interval, and the centered Gram-rank calculation gives the exact endpoint defect. The asymptotic constant follows from evaluating lambda3(c/n). Direct matrix enumeration for n=8,9,10 numerically corroborates the full spectra; it is not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The original Johnson distance has 1-negative type by its binary Hamming realization, but capping only its distance-four pairs destroys that property; four-subsets are the first constant-weight layer where this effect is possible. The theorem classifies the entire infinite family of negative-type exponents, identifies an intrinsically third-degree harmonic obstruction, computes a sharp Euclidean embedding-dimension discontinuity and the dimension-scaled critical constant. Neither a general determinant recipe nor the known Johnson eigenvalue table supplies these specific facts without the new spectral ordering proof.
